# Dishwasher Loading

## Setup

Fill the salt reservoir when the light comes on, using coarse dishwasher salt and a funnel so nothing spills onto the base. Rinse aid goes in the door dispenser, set to about three on the dial. I run the 55 C eco cycle for a normal day, saving the intensive program for baked on trays. Hard water here means the salt matters more than the rinse aid for spotting. I keep the manual page for the salt setting taped inside the cupboard door.

## Cleaning

The filter basket gets rinsed weekly under warm water, and a soft brush clears the fine mesh. I wipe the door seal monthly and run a hot empty cycle with a cup of citric acid every six weeks to keep the interior bright. The spray arms unclip for a soak when the holes look blocked. The cutlery basket goes in the sink with the plates for a scrub now and then.

## Notes

Load the cutlery basket mixed, handles up and down, so spoons do not nest. Bowls go face down in the top rack and glasses between the tines, never over the cutlery basket. Plates sit in the bottom rack facing the centre so the spray reaches the dirty side. Leave space between items; crowding is the usual reason a load comes out gritty. I scrape rather than rinse before loading, and I put sharp knives point down so nobody gets cut lifting them out. The top rack stays for cups, small bowls and the odd plastic tub that would flip in the bottom.
